content.user_title: Make Failing Tests Pass with Minimal TDD Changes
content.value_statement: Developers often add unnecessary complexity while moving from a failing test to a passing test. This skill guides focused implementation and records debt for refactoring.
actual_capabilities: Reviews failing tests and identifies the smallest required behavior.
Guides incremental implementation one failing test at a time.
Applies fake, obvious implementation, and triangulation strategies.
Provides patterns for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, C#, Go, and Ruby.
Checks the full test suite for regressions after implementation.
Documents shortcuts and technical debt for the refactor phase.
limitations: Requires existing failing tests and access to the project test runner.
Does not replace the refactor phase or production hardening.
Does not guarantee that tests fully represent business requirements.
Needs human review for security, performance, and deployment concerns.

use_cases.title: Implement a New Feature
use_cases.description: Turn a focused failing unit test into the smallest passing implementation without adding unrelated behavior.

use_cases.title: Repair a Regression
use_cases.description: Use a reproducible failing test to scope and verify a minimal regression fix.

use_cases.title: Guide TDD Practice
use_cases.description: Teach incremental green-phase decisions with explicit shortcuts and a clear handoff to refactoring.

prompt_templates.title: Pass One Failing Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this failing test and error output. Implement only the behavior required to make this test pass, then explain the change.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has one clear failing test.

prompt_templates.title: Work Through a Test File
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these failing tests. Start with the simplest failure, make one minimal change, and run the relevant tests after each step.
prompt_templates.scenario: Several related tests fail in one module.

prompt_templates.title: Preserve Existing Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Fix this regression using the smallest production-code change. Run the focused test and full suite, then list any deferred technical debt.
prompt_templates.scenario: A mature project needs a controlled regression fix.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Green-Phase Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these failures and choose fake implementation, obvious implementation, or triangulation for each. Implement incrementally and justify every behavior added.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs explicit TDD decision analysis.

output_examples.input: A price test expects a validation error for negative values.
output_examples.output: Added the smallest negative-price check in the model. The focused tests and full suite pass. Broader pricing rules remain deferred.

output_examples.input: A task endpoint test expects status 201 and a returned identifier.
output: Added a minimal create route with in-memory storage.
Verified the endpoint test and existing suite.
Deferred persistence, advanced validation, and service extraction.

output_examples.input: A user service has three failures that reveal repeated hard-coded behavior.
output_examples.output: Replaced the hard-coded result with a small in-memory map after triangulation. All tests pass, and database integration remains refactor work.

best_practices: Start with the simplest failing test and change one behavior at a time.
Run focused tests after each change and the full suite before completion.
Record shortcuts, assumptions, and technical debt for the refactor phase.
anti_patterns: Do not add features, abstractions, or validation that tests do not require.
Do not disable, weaken, or bypass tests to obtain a green result.
Do not treat minimal green-phase code as production-ready without review.

faq.question: What is the TDD green phase?
faq.answer: It is the step where developers write the smallest implementation that makes a failing test pass.

faq.question: Does this skill write tests?
faq.answer: No. It expects failing tests created during the red phase and focuses on production code.

faq.question: Will it refactor the implementation?
faq.answer: No. It records refactoring needs but keeps green-phase changes minimal and behavior-focused.

faq.question: Which languages does it support?
faq.answer: Its playbook includes patterns for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, C#, Go, and Ruby.

faq.question: Does it run the full test suite?
faq.answer: It instructs the agent to run focused tests after changes and the full suite before completion.

faq.question: Can minimal code be used in production?
faq.answer: Only after review and refactoring address security, validation, performance, persistence, and operational requirements.
